model_priors.model_reasoning: ERBB2 (HER2) is a well-characterized receptor tyrosine kinase. Unlike EGFR (ERBB1), ERBB2 lacks a high-affinity direct ligand and is primarily activated as a co-receptor. Its basal/constitutive internalization rate is significantly slower than EGFR. ERBB2 is known to recycle efficiently and accumulates at the plasma membrane at high steady-state levels, partly because it lacks strong ubiquitination signals and has reduced CBL-mediated downregulation compared to EGFR. However, it does internalize constitutively — it is not a static surface protein. The cytoplasmic tail contains several tyrosine-based motifs and a dileucine-like sequence, and ERBB2 can be internalized via clathrin-mediated endocytosis, though more slowly and with more efficient recycling than EGFR. The net result is a moderate internalization propensity with a large steady-state surface pool — consistent with the well-documented difficulty of achieving efficient ERBB2 downregulation compared to EGFR. This is the canonical isoform; only one isoform is provided.

per_isoform.topology_summary: Signal peptide (21 aa); single-pass type I transmembrane protein; N-terminus extracellular (~632 aa), C-terminus cytoplasmic (~581 aa).
per_isoform.endocytic_motifs_noted: Cytoplasmic tail (residues ~676–1255) contains multiple tyrosine-based motifs (e.g., YXXΦ candidates including Y877, Y1005, Y1112, Y1127, Y1139, Y1196, Y1221, Y1222, Y1248) and potential dileucine-like sequences. However, ERBB2 is notably resistant to CBL-mediated ubiquitination and lysosomal targeting compared to EGFR, limiting efficient downregulation. No canonical NPXY motif identified. The long cytoplasmic tail provides multiple potential adaptor-binding sites.
per_isoform.rationale: ERBB2 internalizes constitutively via clathrin-mediated endocytosis but at a substantially slower rate than EGFR. It lacks a direct high-affinity ligand, has reduced CBL/ubiquitin-mediated lysosomal routing, and recycles efficiently back to the plasma membrane. The result is a large, stable surface pool at steady state — a hallmark of moderate rather than high internalization propensity. The protein is not a static surface resident (it does turn over), but the balance strongly favors surface accumulation. This is well-established in the ERBB2/HER2 trafficking literature and is consistent with the sequence features: a long cytoplasmic tail with tyrosine motifs that can engage clathrin machinery, but without the strong ubiquitination/downregulation signals that drive rapid EGFR internalization and degradation.

basal.rationale: Multiple evidence clips note that HER2 is innately stable at the plasma membrane and internalizes poorly without stimulation. int_evi_07 explicitly states that multivalent ligands 'largely overcome the innate stability of HER2 in the plasma membrane,' implying low constitutive internalization. int_evi_09 shows that in vivo, cell-associated anti-HER2 is primarily receptor-bound with minimal pinocytosed mAb, consistent with slow basal turnover.

native_ligand.rationale: No evidence clips in the ledger directly measure HER2 internalization driven by its endogenous ligands (e.g., heregulin/NRG1).

therapeutic.rationale: Multiple clips document HER2 internalization driven by therapeutic binders (T-DXd, T-DM1, pertuzumab-PEG6-DM1, anti-HER2 antibodies). Internalization is HER2 density-dependent (int_evi_01, int_evi_06), modulated by EGFR co-expression (int_evi_02–05), and proceeds primarily via clathrin-mediated endocytosis for trastuzumab-based ADCs (int_evi_08), though multivalent affibody ligands can redirect to clathrin-independent aggregation-dependent endocytosis (int_evi_07). In vivo SPECT modeling shows specific receptor-mediated internalization with peak receptor occupancy of 35% at 13 h (int_evi_09). The rate is meaningful but context-dependent and suppressible by EGFR overexpression, supporting a moderate rather than uniformly high grade.

literature.rationale: HER2 internalizes at a moderate rate when engaged by therapeutic antibodies or ADCs, with efficiency strongly dependent on HER2 surface density and modulated by EGFR co-expression. Basal internalization is low due to the receptor's innate plasma membrane stability. No native-ligand internalization data are present in the ledger. The therapeutic mode is the best-supported and most delivery-relevant, justifying an overall moderate grade.
literature.cross_condition_note: Internalization rate is substantially higher in HER2-high cells (e.g., HCC1954) than HER2-medium or HER2-low lines, and is suppressed 1.3–1.5-fold by EGFR overexpression in CRC lines; multivalent affibody-based ligands bypass the clathrin pathway and achieve more robust internalization than trastuzumab-based ADCs in cells with compromised CME.

sources.claim: Decreases in HER2 expression in isogenic model systems corresponded to reductions in T-DXd internalization, directly linking HER2 surface levels to ADC uptake efficiency.

source.title: Trastuzumab Deruxtecan Resistance via Loss of HER2 Expression and Binding

spans.quote: Using isogenic model systems, we demonstrated that decreases in HER2 expression corresponded to reductions in T-DXd internalization and major increases in drug IC50 value for tumor growth inhibition.

sources.claim: Elevated EGFR expression promotes EGFR/HER2 heterodimer formation and suppresses T-DXd internalization and efficacy, demonstrating that EGFR modulates HER2 endocytosis.

source.title: EGFR-directed antibodies promote HER2 ADC internalization and efficacy

spans.quote: We demonstrate that elevated EGFR expression levels can promote EGFR/HER2 heterodimer formation and suppress T-DXd internalization and efficacy.

sources.claim: Knockdown of EGFR expression or pharmacologic stimulation of EGFR endocytosis with EGFR monoclonal antibodies restores T-DXd (HER2-ADC) trafficking and antitumor activity in EGFR-overexpressing cancers in vivo.

spans.quote: Knockdown of EGFR expression or pharmacologic stimulation of EGFR endocytosis with EGFR monoclonal antibodies restores T-DXd trafficking and antitumor activity in EGFR-overexpressing cancers in vivo.

source.title: EGFR-directed antibodies promote HER2 ADC internalization and efficacy

spans.quote: In a HER2-positive EGFR -amplified CRC cell line DiFi, knockdown of EGFR increased the rate of T-DXd internalization 1.5-fold compared to the non-targeting control ( Figure 1 C and Video S1 ).

sources.claim: Overexpression of EGFR in EGFR-low CRC cell lines NCI-H508 or HCA46 suppressed T-DXd (HER2-ADC) internalization rate 1.4-fold or 1.3-fold, respectively, compared to empty vector control, measured by pH-sensitive dye assay.

spans.quote: Moreover, overexpression of EGFR in EGFR-low CRC cell lines NCI-H508 or HCA46 suppressed T-DXd internalization rate 1.4-fold or 1.3-fold, respectively, compared to the empty vector (EV) control ( Figure 1 F and Video S2 and Figure S1 A).

sources.claim: Internalization of pertuzumab-PEG6-DM1 (anti-HER2 ADC) in HCC1954 and JIMT-1 cells was HER2 density-dependent, with the conjugate showing 2.5–22-fold higher internalization than unconjugated pertuzumab.

source.title: Potency and safety of novel [<sup>225</sup>Ac]Ac-labeled pertuzumab-PEGylated emtansine drug conjugate against HER2-positive breast cancer

spans.quote:
Safety and biodistribution were carried out in healthy female Balb/C mice and in mice bearing HCC1954/JIMT-1 xenografts, respectively. Radioimmunotherapy was done in nude mice bearing trastuzumab-resistant HCC1954 (high HER2-density), T-DM1/trastuzumab-resistant JIMT-1 (medium HER2-density) and MDA-MB-468 (negative control with very low HER2-density) xenografts.

Results

Internalisation in HCC1954 and JIMT-1 cells was HER2 density-dependent, with pertuzumab-PEG6-DM1 2.5-22-fold higher than unconjugated pertuzumab.

sources.claim: Compartmental modeling of SPECT imaging data demonstrated that cell-associated anti-HER2 was primarily receptor-bound, with a peak receptor occupancy of 35% at 13 h post administration of a 10 mg/kg dose, with minimal free and pinocytosed mAb, characterizing HER2-mediated internalization kinetics in vivo.

source.title: Measurement of specific and nonspecific tissue uptake of antibodies in tumor by SPECT imaging and nonlinear compartmental modeling

spans.quote:
Compartmental modeling of the SPECT data demonstrated that cell-associated anti-HER2 was primarily receptor-bound, with a peak receptor occupancy of 35% at 13 h post administration of a 10 mg/kg dose, with minimal free and pinocytosed mAb.

Conclusion

Here, we successfully developed an imaging and modeling approach to capture anti-HER2 antibody receptor binding as well as specific and nonspecific internalization over time in vivo.
